# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-329 @ `2e78c76`, TIER 2 through-code) | **GO-with-findings — 6 tamper classes caught, 10 MISSED, each proved on the wire from a booted server; and it found the stronger instrument was already in the next file** (2026-09-07 18:54) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Applied Wednesday's standing line exactly — *narrow, not fake, hence GO-with-findings*. **F-2 is the keeper: the "belt-and-braces" deny-list is NOT a second layer** — it shares the allow-list's parser; on tamper E `nodeVersion` is ON the deny-list, went out on the wire, and **both cells stayed green**. *"Two layers that fail together are one layer"* — and the commit message presents them as independent. **The one thing it would change:** the builder's note called source-reading "the strongest instrument available without booting the app" — true as worded, **but this repo ALREADY boots the app** (`__tests__/erasure-health-branches.test.js:97-143` spawns the real server on a reserved port); rebuilt on that pattern it **caught 7 of the 10 misses.** Ten misses each `node --check` clean and read off the wire, incl. a full spread leaking `persistence.dataDir`, an allowed KEY with a sensitive VALUE, and two keys on one physical line defeating a line-anchored regex. **Credited the builder honestly:** its CONTROL asserts the tamper landed BEFORE asserting the effect — the check RD-362's control lacked — and named L and N as limits of BOTH instruments, not just the builder's. |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-969 item 1 / PR #892 @ `f54b2dce1`, TIER 2) | **NO GO on a BLOCKER: the fix REPRODUCED ITS OWN TICKET'S DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **F1:** on a machine without `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — **the normal state of a clean stack per KS-915, and the case the builder's OWN design note cites** — the step reports a green `PROVISIONED`, writes a manifest where **all five actors collapse to `OWNER`**, and **that manifest OUTRANKS the correctly-roled seeded accounts in every consumer.** So the PR switches every wired suite to wrongly-roled identities **by default and calls it success** — *"the silent-fallback shape the ticket exists to remove, reproduced one level up."* **F2 answered the question the brief turned on, and answered it bigger: a bypass CLASS, not a bypass** — `run.py integration` 0 pre-suite lines with **17 live httpx cells run**; playwright `test:debug` 0 lines with **30+ live specs enumerated** — each measured under an identical env **against a working control in the same project, so a zero is a real bypass and not a blind instrument.** **F3: the strict flag fails OPEN, silently, on every spelling but literal `"1"`** (`"TRUE"`, `" true"`, `"01"`, even `"1 "`), with **no warning that the value was unrecognised** — and the repo's own `parseBoolean` lowercases and trims, so the module disagrees with its own codebase. **It RAN the schemathesis arm** rather than inferring it. **It VERIFIED the builder's design call (b)** and judged (a) *"defensible; the reasoning is wrong"* — separating a correct decision from a wrong justification. **🔴 AND IT CORRECTED WEDNESDAY'S SEVERITY CALL, precisely and fairly:** the brief said a defect here *"breaks or silently skips testing"*; its correction — *"F1 does not skip testing. It silently changes the identity every wired suite runs as, to a less-correct one, and reports success. Not 'less coverage'; coverage that asserts the wrong thing while looking healthy."* **It kept the TIER at 2 and corrected only the CEILING**, which is the right distinction. **Stated at equal prominence that F1 was proved agains
